def probe_fingerprint() -> str:
    """A digest of the instrument, so a stale verdict cannot be reused.

    `runs/027_reactivity.json` was produced by a **10**-perturbation probe.
    `market:one_price` was added the next day, `SCHEMA` did not move, and
    nothing in the repository could tell that the committed population table and
    the current instrument disagreed -- so a third-party agent sat in
    `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` as `closed_loop` while the tool at HEAD called it
    `market_reactive`, and that stale sentence is what scoped Phase 0C.

    The first version of this digest covered perturbation **names** and the
    source of `probe`.  A reviewer measured what that misses: gutting
    `_halve_prices` to a no-op, replacing `observations`, and changing
    `COVERAGE_TIER` all left the digest **unchanged**, so only the exact
    historical accident (a perturbation *added*) was caught.  F17 says the digest
    must come from the instrument itself "so that forgetting is not an available
    failure", and forgetting was still available in three directions.

    So the digest covers every part that can change a verdict: each
    perturbation's NAME, GROUP and BODY; the functions that decide which callable
    runs and what it is asked (`load_agent`, `observations`, `call_agent`,
    `canonical`, `is_inert`); the classifier (`probe`); the exact sampled steps;
    and the tier constants that turn a count into a class.
    Editing a comment inside any of them invalidates it, which is the
    conservative direction -- re-measuring is one command, and a stale verdict is
    not detectable by any other means.
    """
    import inspect
